ateret-zekenim/1:ב: And even if he returned and deposited it with another non-Jew, etc. — Hagahot Alfasi, beginning of Pesachim. And it appears to me that this is certainly obvious: if from the outset the non-Jew placed his chametz in the non-Jew's domain and there the Jew accepted liability, he need not destroy it, as Beit Yosef wrote that if he designated for him a corner, etc. — all the more so here, where from the outset he placed his chametz there even though the Jew accepted liability; and one may bring many proofs on this. And if he is not liable for it he is not obligated to destroy it, and he must make before him a partition ten handbreadths high; even if he designated a place for him one should be stringent and requires a partition ten handbreadths — Maharitz wrote, and this is his language in Machloket Michtav Michtav Kodesh: it appears to me one may not bring proof at all from there, for there the owner of the chametz is a Jew; if so, conversely there is room for concern for a weekday, etc. — if he does not say to the owners "here is yours before you" but the robber pays the owners in exchange for his chametz, then the owners of the chametz would have benefit from chametz that passed over Passover since they receive payment from the robber for his chametz; therefore we say he tells him "here is yours before you — go take your chametz," etc. — the robber would fulfill biur chametz and when burned he would pay as for lost property and there would be no concern that owners have benefit in the chametz through payment to them since the chametz is not in existence; the robber does not wish this and says conversely to the owners "here is the mitzvah of biur chametz before you and you fulfill it," etc. — not so here in our case, where if the Jew returns to the non-Jew he does not fulfill biur chametz and the Jew has benefit in returning the chametz to the non-Jew so he need not pay; and in truth there is no prohibition of benefit — understand well.
baer-heitev/1:א: He must destroy it. And if he transgressed and did not destroy it — Magen Avraham wrote: if the non-Jew comes after Passover he may give him the chametz; nevertheless some say it is forbidden from this reason to give it to him lest the non-Jew return and sell it to a Jew and the Jew stumble on chametz that passed over Passover — see there. And Kaf HaChayim disagrees and wrote he may say to him "here is yours before you" — see there; and see responsum Shevut Yaakov chelek 2 siman 66.
baer-heitev/1:ב: Another non-Jew. And if the second non-Jew accepted liability for theft and loss — permitted, Magen Avraham. And Kaf HaChayim disagrees and is stringent — see Peri Chadash. And if he deposited it with its owner — permitted; and likewise if the non-Jew placed his chametz in a non-Jew's domain and there a Jew accepted liability — agreement of the Poskim.
baer-heitev/1:ג: And there are those who disagree. And b'dieved one may rely on the first view. (And likewise Kaf HaChayim agreed there.) And if he is liable by law of the kingdom he is obligated to destroy according to all — Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/2:א: He is not obligated to destroy it. But on Passover he may not accept any deposit of chametz even without any liability at all — Kaf HaChayim.
baer-heitev/2:ג: But if it is before Yom Tov. And likewise on chol ha'moed he must make a partition even though he will take it tomorrow; but if he left it only half a day one may be lenient with covering a vessel — Magen Avraham. And Kaf HaChayim wrote he destroys it if he is not obligated to pay the non-Jew and need not trouble to make a partition on chol ha'moed — see there.
baer-heitev/4:_: Also the depositor. See Kaf HaChayim and in responsum Chacham Tzvi siman 39 and responsum Panim Me'irot siman 46.
beer-hagolah/4:ב: Thus it is evident from his words, for he wrote in seif 1 that if the guardian accepted liability he transgresses regarding it and must destroy it; and likewise ruled Bach there.
beur-hagra/1:א: Seif 1 — a non-Jew who deposited, etc. He omitted the law of designating a house for him, etc., because he holds like Ran's explanation that an unspecified deposit is as stored, etc.; and it requires study, for behold from the exclusion of a Jew from guarding, as written in Choshen Mishpat siman 301 seif 9 — see Tosafot Shabbat 44a s.v. shomer; and likewise it is difficult on the Rosh who wrote from here forty, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ב: Theft and loss. Rambam and Rosh in the name of R' Yitzchak, and as written in the Gemara "if it is stolen or lost," etc. And according to Rama in Choshen Mishpat siman 72 seif 2 it must be specifically for unavoidable accidents, as Tosafot wrote there s.v. ha; and even though in Pesachim there they wrote "the whole sugya," etc. — meaning in an unspecified case where they did not accept explicitly; but unspecified liability as a pledge is presumably liable.
beur-hagra/1:ד: And even if he returned, etc. Magen Avraham, and as written in the Gemara it is like going — and so is the halachah; but in the owner's hand — permitted, as Magen Avraham wrote, and so is implied in the Gemara that they spoke only of receiving deposits and accepting liability.
beur-hagra/1:ה: And there are those who say even, etc. That stolen or lost — no, as Rosh wrote there, and their proof from what is written there "deposited with him" and an unspecified deposit is an unpaid guardian — all the more so according to Rashi's explanation that designating a house without accepting liability is discussed. And Ran's explanation of his words "deposited with him" — since he received it in his domain it is as his, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ו: And even if, etc. There "in his city is stringent," etc. — "if it is stolen," etc.; and by law he does not become a guardian for the Jew, as written in Choshen Mishpat siman 301 seif 9; and likewise what is written "deposited with him," etc., is also in such a case — with this the difficulty on the Rosh is resolved; and his words are wondrous from what he wrote that an unspecified, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ז: And there are those who disagree. Raavad, who holds that these payments were by law and that the law of the kingdom was upon them.
beur-hagra/2:א: Seif 2 — and he must make. As Rashi explained s.v. chametzo — without accepting liability it follows his view that with liability designation does not help; and so Rambam and Rif, not like Ramban; and in any case who holds that even with liability it helps, who holds like R' Tam in Tosafot there s.v. yichad — that according to his explanation with liability, etc.
beur-hagra/2:ב: And a Jew who left, etc. And specifically, etc. Gemara there "one who finds," etc. chametzo, etc. — and it implies that one who finds even a Jew's chametz, since it says "if of hekdesh"; see Rashi s.v. oseh.
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3 — non-Jew. There the baraita "non-Jew," etc. — see Rashi s.v. ein zokek, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ג: And even. See Magen Avraham and see in chapter 4 of Avodah Zarah 59a; therefore even though from the beginning of Rashba's words it implies specifically when they eat together, but according to what he forbade even with a separating cloth there is no distinction — therefore unspecified in Shulchan Aruch.
beur-hagra/4:א: Seif 4 — a Jew who deposited. As written "there are those who say" in seif 1; but a Jew, etc. s.v. over; and although Tosafot there 2 s.v. shekoneh wrote "the whole sugya," etc. — they wrote only regarding a Jew's chametz, and so is implied there from the challenge from the mishnah to Rava "we learned a Jew," etc., and it does not say the mishnah is when he accepted liability.
beur-hagra/4:ב: He transgresses regarding it. Apparently proof from the mishnah "a Jew who lent to a Jew," etc., and we establish it even though we deposited with him — specifically when he said from now; and even though one may reject that the mishnah is when he did not accept liability, similar to a Jew who lent, as Tosafot wrote — nevertheless since the Gemara was forced and did not establish, etc.
biur-halacha/1:_: If he is liable for it. See Magen Avraham and Mishna Berurah there that even if he designated a corner for him in his house he must destroy if he accepted liability; and if he did not accept liability he must make a partition.
biur-halacha/2:_: And he must make a partition. See there in Mishna Berurah that a cloth partition does not suffice because they go back and forth beneath it; and covering with a vessel does not suffice for all of Passover as one may remove the vessel — see there at length.
biur-halacha/4:_: Even the depositor transgresses. See Mishna Berurah there at length; and the essential law is that the Torah obligated biur only when the chametz is in the Jew's domain as his property — see there.
chatam-sofer/1:_: If he is liable. We are in Babylon — meaning monetary law; and there is no law of guardianship for a non-Jew. And even though he is liable by kingdom law he is not liable to me for theft, but in the case of a resident convert he needs a partition because he is under the Jew's control.
chatam-sofer/2:_: And he must make a partition. There is no name of Heaven here; and as a result of kingdom law he is liable to pay — there is no liability for theft, and it is not seen before him as chametz of a Jew.
chok-yaakov/1:א: If he is liable for it. Thus is Tur's language; however Rambam in chapter 4 wrote "if he accepted liability," and so Rashi in the first chapter of Pesachim — implying we require explicit acceptance of liability; but from silence it is as if he did not accept liability, and so Levush; however Ran brought in Beit Yosef that from silence it is as accepted, etc.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: He must destroy it. And if he transgressed and did not destroy — Magen Avraham wrote: if the non-Jew comes after Passover he may give him the chametz, as we say regarding one who stole chametz and Passover passed: "here is yours before you"; nevertheless some forbid from this reason lest the non-Jew return and sell to a Jew, etc.
chok-yaakov/1:ה: And even if he returned and deposited it. It implies even if he deposited it again as the first non-Jew deposited with a Jew with the Jew's liability — he returned and deposited with the non-Jew on his liability — nevertheless the Jew must destroy since it is as his own, as chametz of a Jew deposited with a non-Jew.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: With another non-Jew. And Magen Avraham wrote: from his precision "with another non-Jew" it implies that if he returned and deposited with this non-Jew, even though liability is on the Jew, he is not obligated to destroy — as with accepting liability for non-Jew's chametz in a non-Jew's house; even those who disagree with R' Tam agree here.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: And there are those who disagree. And the view of great Poskim is as the first view, and it is primary; and if he is liable by kingdom law, even per the disagreeing view he is obligated to destroy, as explained in Raavad and Magen Avraham — see Beit Yosef.
chok-yaakov/2:א: He is not obligated to destroy it. But on Passover he may not accept any deposit of chametz even without liability at all — so Rokeach siman 167; and if a non-Jew left chametz without permission it is explained in the gloss how he should conduct himself.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: A partition ten handbreadths high. And Magen Avraham wrote one should not make a partition with a cloth because they go beneath it; and that covering a vessel does not suffice here because he does this all Passover days and sometimes they remove the vessel for use — therefore covering a vessel does not suffice, as Rashi explained.
chok-yaakov/2:ג: But if it is before Yom Tov. For one can make a partition — unlike Yom Tov which is only one day where covering a vessel suffices and a partition is impossible because moving it is forbidden — therefore covering a vessel suffices; and if on chol ha'moed he may move it and throw it out, etc.
chok-yaakov/3:א: He is not required to remove him. And he concluded in Shulchan Aruch klal 7 siman 62: what they practice of rebuking a non-Jew entering a Jew's domain — lest crumbs fall from his hand and sometimes he come to a prohibition through them.
chok-yaakov/3:ב: To bring it onto the table with him. Meaning they should not eat together at one table lest chametz mix into the Jew's food.
chok-yaakov/4:_: Even though he accepted liability. For nevertheless the money belongs to him; and we did not say above in seif 1 that accepting liability makes it as his own except for this matter — through accepting liability he has connection and right in it though it is not essentially his; because of this right the Torah obligated him in biur; but conversely when the thing is his and another accepted liability, there is no reason to say the chametz left his domain through another's acceptance of liability.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 — if he is liable, etc. The language of the Tur is that he is liable for theft and loss whether in his house or anywhere in his domain; and Rambam wrote similarly. And the Ramban wrote at length that the law of a Jew's chametz deposited with a non-Jew is more stringent than non-Jew's chametz with a Jew — see his words there.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: He must destroy it. And if he transgressed and did not destroy — some say after Passover he may return it to the non-Jew; and some forbid — see there at length.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: And he must make a partition. See Magen Avraham; and on Yom Tov covering a vessel is better than a cloth partition because the cloth goes back and forth beneath it.
eshel-avraham/1:א: If he is liable. Meaning explicitly for theft and loss; but from silence for negligence alone one should be stringent l'chatchila to destroy, as below in Mishna Berurah.
eshel-avraham/1:ג: In his domain. Even in another's house in his domain — if he accepted liability he must destroy; if not, a partition.
eshel-avraham/3:_: He is not required to remove him. For the chametz is in the non-Jew's hand and he guards it.
eshel-avraham/4:_: Even the depositor. For he caused the prohibition; and even though the guardian accepted liability, the depositor also transgresses because he removed it from his domain while it remains his money.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] If he is liable, etc. — the Jew must destroy when he accepted liability for theft and loss; see Poskim at length.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) [Seif 2] If he is not liable, etc. — he makes a partition; on Yom Tov he covers with a vessel; before Yom Tov a partition — see Mishna Berurah.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) [Seif 3] He is not required to remove him — for the non-Jew guards his chametz; but forbidden to eat together on one table — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: In Shulchan Aruch seif 1 — non-Jew, etc. If he is liable for it — Kaf HaChayim infers he must accept liability explicitly (and this is what helps); otherwise there is no law of guardians for a gentile, as the verse "his fellow" excludes, as in Choshen Mishpat siman 301; and he wrote further that according to those who say even an unpaid guardian must destroy — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And according to those who say in Choshen Mishpat that even when not liable by laws of guardianship he is liable for negligence — likewise here he must destroy at present; and it must be said that this view, who holds he is liable for negligence, is Rambam's view — he gave a reason: although exempt from all laws of guardianship, for negligence he is liable as a damager; thus what he is liable for in negligence is not because he became a guardian but because he damaged; therefore even if liable for negligence per this view he need not destroy since he did not become a guardian and it is not called his chametz nor is he liable for it. However, per Shach in siman 66 s.k. 126 to resolve Raavad's challenge on owners' negligence — Rambam does not mean actual damager but obligated by logic without a verse for negligence; therefore we do not exclude negligence from "his fellow" — see there at length; and thus in truth what he is liable for in negligence is by law of guardianship; and well one may say he must destroy per those who say an unpaid guardian must destroy.
machatzit-hashekel/4:_: (s.k. 4) On Yom Tov, etc. — as written in siman 315 that any partition not made to permit something may be made on Shabbat.
magen-avraham/1:_: With another non-Jew. Who is not its owner — for it is as his own and it is as a Jew depositing chametz with a non-Jew — Shach; and it implies if he deposited with its owner he does not transgress; and in Choshen Mishpat siman 72 seif 3 — even if he returned and deposited with its owner, if the first is liable for theft and loss — see there; nevertheless it is as accepting liability for non-Jew's chametz in a non-Jew's house — permitted, as Tur in the name of R' Tam — see there; and although we do not rule like R' Tam, that is when the Jew designated a corner in his house, but in the non-Jew's house all permit. And if the Jew deposited with another non-Jew and the second non-Jew accepted liability — it appears permitted, for some say even a Jew's chametz deposited with a non-Jew with the non-Jew's acceptance is permitted; and although we do not rule thus, nevertheless for non-Jew's chametz it is permitted as above; however the gentile must accept liability for theft and loss; and even though the non-Jew claims from the Jew and the Jew claims from the second non-Jew — it does not help; and in any case where the Jew must destroy and transgressed and did not destroy — if the non-Jew comes after Passover he may give him the chametz, for chametz that passed Passover is forbidden only as a penalty and they did not penalize in this; so Choshen Mishpat siman 363 — one who stole chametz and Passover passed: "here is yours before you," and if lost he pays its value — thus he benefits in returning the chametz; nevertheless permitted; likewise here; and possibly even if the non-Jew comes during Passover he may leave it for him to take, for we say regarding prohibited benefit "here is yours before you" in Bava Kamma 98a; nevertheless some forbid from this reason to give the non-Jew lest he return and sell to a Jew — and so Hagahot Maimoniot end of chapter 5 Chametz and siman 467.
magen-avraham/2:ב: So that he not forget. Because one is not accustomed to avoid it all year — unlike other prohibitions where no partition is needed because one is accustomed to avoid them.
magen-avraham/2:ד: Before Yom Tov. And if he left it on chol ha'moed he must make a partition — as Rashi's language, even if he will take it tomorrow; but if he left it only half a day one may be lenient with covering a vessel.
magen-avraham/3:ב: And even with a separating cloth. And even though if one eats meat and one milk at one table it is permitted with a separating cloth — here since chametz is significant it is impossible that a crumb of the non-Jew's not mix into the Jew's food and it is forbidden; and Acharonim agreed that even if he has no acquaintance with this non-Jew and no concern he might forget and eat from his chametz — likewise forbidden, for perhaps a crumb of chametz mixes by itself into the Jew's food. And all this when they eat at one time; but when the Jew is not eating he may leave the non-Jew to eat at his table only that the Jew should clean the table well after the non-Jew eats so no crumbs remain; and he should be careful when the non-Jew leaves his house to take all his chametz and leave nothing — see below siman 88 and siman 423.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) Liable for it, etc. — when he explicitly accepted liability and kinyan was made from his hand; otherwise there is no law of guardians for a non-Jew, as explained in Choshen Mishpat siman 301 seif 1 and seif 4. And if kingdom law makes him liable even without specification, from the moment he becomes a guardian it is in the Jew's domain even without stipulating liability for theft — as explained below.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) Anywhere in his domain — even if he rented or lent him a place by itself for his chametz in his house or courtyard it does not help if he accepted liability, for we hold rental does not acquire; thus the chametz remains in the Jew's house. Nevertheless b'dieved if he kept the chametz with him until after Passover one may rely on Poskim who hold that where he designated a place for his chametz he does not transgress bal yera'eh even if he accepted liability, for we require chametz under the Jew's hand as an ordinary deposit under his domain to move and place anywhere; and if he designated a place by itself it is not called present and the chametz is permitted to eat and benefit. Designating a place is when he designates before him a house, room, or corner in his house by rental or loan; but if he received a deposit without designation and afterward designated a place without the non-Jew depositor's knowledge it does not help, lest the non-Jew does not want it placed except in the Jew's domain; and even making a partition does not help.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) He must destroy it — at the time of biur if the non-Jew is not here to return it; and whether nullification and sale help like his own chametz — Acharonim disagree, many stringent since the body is not his; many lenient (see Sedei Chemed ma'arechet chametz umatzah siman 5 ot 33). Per Magen Avraham in s.k. 1 there is a remedy: return and deposit with another non-Jew or sell the house where the chametz rests to the non-Jew who accepts liability for theft and loss; best to do both — sell the house and sell the chametz.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) And even if he returned and deposited, etc. — for it is as his own since he accepted liability; thus it is as a Jew depositing chametz with a non-Jew — forbidden, as in seif 4. And even if the other non-Jew accepted all liability that was on the Jew — nevertheless forbidden, for liability did not leave the Jew regarding the first non-Jew; some are lenient since the body is not his and not in his house; and per their view likewise when he sold the room where the chametz rests it is permitted if this non-Jew accepted liability for theft and loss — Peri Megadim.
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (8) And there are those who say, etc. — l'chatchila one should be concerned for this view; therefore if the non-Jew depositor is before him he must return to him; if the non-Jew is not here he should sell the chametz and also nullify (and although many Poskim hold sale and nullification do not help for chametz that is not his body, in such a case one may rely on the lenient); but b'dieved when the hour arrived that he cannot sell to the non-Jew as explained in siman 443, one may rely on the first reasoning and the Jew is not obligated to destroy from the world but may keep this chametz until the non-Jew owner comes to the city — even if he comes during Passover he returns his chametz immediately on arrival to remove Torah prohibition concern in this retention per the first view (only beware not to touch with his hands as in siman 444); and after Passover it is permitted to eat from it even if not returned to its owner.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (9) And there are those who disagree — since the Jew did not accept liability and is exempt by Torah and kingdom law, the chametz is not considered his through compelling the non-Jew. Nevertheless the primary view is the first; see above s.k. 4; and if he transgressed and did not destroy and Passover passed, one need not be stringent even for eating — permitted.
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (18) And even with a separating cloth — and even if he does not say the berachah with the kohanim it is forbidden, for obviously a berachah le'vatalah is forbidden — Torah said to bless to kohanim not Israelites, as in previous note; likewise Eliyah Rabbah note 4. And all this when eating at one time; but when not eating he may leave the non-Jew to eat at his table only he must clean the table well after the non-Jew eats so no crumbs remain; and beware when the non-Jew leaves his house to take all his chametz and leave nothing.
peri-megadim/1:א: Rather — Taz challenged Rambam's explanation: why does the Gemara need a verse; one may say since he holds gorem lemamon is as money, likewise for unavoidable loss — otherwise per those who hold not as money, whence this; and also for seif 4 since it returned to sight, etc. And his challenge on "in his city is stringent" — selling is difficult for it is not his; and giving to another non-Jew does not suffice especially per Rama; Magen Avraham note 1 will be explained; see Mishneh Lemelech and Levushei Serad's answer regarding kingdom law — see there at length.
peri-megadim/1:ב: And behold the Mechaber brought the first view in unspecified form — only theft, not negligence like Rambam and R' Yitzchak; and he did not decide regarding unavoidable loss — thus after Passover one may say it is a doubt for leniency; within Passover a Torah doubt; if the loss is only from negligence within Passover — double doubt; all the more for first view in unspecified form; and to accept l'chatchila — one should not create double doubt with hands — Magen Avraham siman 467; Levush may be explained thus — see there.
peri-megadim/1:ג: I was asked: non-Jews place flour with a Jew in a house, pay fixed weekly rent, and the Jew has liability on Passover — how should they conduct? I answered: sell to them — he has no other remedy; some say semag siman 62 one may benefit a person without his knowledge and make him an agent; or the depositor gives permission to his seller; or deposit with another non-Jew who accepts liability as Magen Avraham note 1; and the place is rented to him — not chametz rent — siman 448; here more lenient; see Magen Avraham further. Our flour is wheat for preserves and full chametz — nullification does not help since it is not his.
peri-megadim/2:_: And one must — Taz: Rashi and R' Tam Pesachim 6a disagree on two matters: Rashi — with liability designation of a corner does not help (Magen Avraham 1); without liability no corner needed but partition rabbinically for seven days for recognition; covering a vessel Rashi answered for one day or Yom Tov when partition impossible; R' Tam — designating a corner with liability permitted, for non-Jew's chametz in his house with Jew's liability is permitted; partition is as his house — before the non-Jew owner; without liability covering a vessel suffices even seven days. They also dispute explanation of designation — Rashi "here is the house" without liability; Tosafot — corner specifically. Taz's "he must pay" should read "must destroy." Halachah follows Rashi as in Shulchan Aruch — see Ran and Bach on Rashi s.v. deposited and accepted liability — see there.
peri-megadim/3:_: But — Taz and likewise Magen Avraham 5 and Rashi Pesachim 6a s.v. oseh — two distinctions: on Yom Tov impossible; on chol ha'moed even half a day needs partition; or because one day need not destroy he destroys — from hour to hour needs partition. Rashi "for all seven" is Levush; Chok Yaakov note 11. "Specifically left without permission" — to accept l'chatchila even on Yom Tov is forbidden as Tosafot Yom Tov — see Magen Avraham; see Bach on Rashi.
peri-megadim/4:א: Israel — Taz: I have material here; the examiner in Ramban Vayikra 12 and Ran Pesachim explains they hold a Jew's chametz in a non-Jew's house or with a friend — even if the guardian did not accept liability the depositor does not transgress "your boundary" parallel to "your houses" which excludes — Ran wrote Rambam Choshen Mishpat 1b wrote Jew's chametz in non-Jew's hand transgresses and he did not know whence — perhaps Ran means only with liability; perhaps Rambam only theft and loss — see Beit Yosef; here likewise depositor; Raavan 6a brought geonim: Jew depositing with non-Jew or Jew with acceptance — guardian liable not depositor since not in his domain; primary reason — not actually in his domain and guardian did not accept — both do not transgress; acceptance not explicit — there unpaid guardian; Rosh ruled guardian must destroy — Tur wrote geonim: since guardian accepted liability — Beit Yosef: Ramban and Ran; what ended Rosh "since he deposited his house we call it his house" — difficult; Netiv Chayim chelek 5 daf 45 — if Jew's chametz with non-Jew and transgressed — geonim say if guardian accepted liability depositor does not transgress; majority hold depositor must destroy; for geonim require two things: guardian accepted and placed in his domain not depositor's — then depositor does not transgress as Tur; majority — depositor as guardian both liable; Levush distinguishes non-Jew's deposit guardian transgresses vs Jew's chametz guardian does not — see Taz 1. Ramban and Ran explain like R' Tam — designated house with liability permitted — Jew's chametz in non-Jew's house why no transgress (excluded from your houses) — rabbinically forbidden; Jew who lent to non-Jew after Passover transgresses as below; non-Jew's chametz in non-Jew's house with Jew's liability — even rabbinically no transgress; R' Tam s.v. yichad — not found except not present and not from your houses; baraita concludes teach us not found; Rosh — Jew's chametz in non-Jew's house with liability — depositor transgresses; non-Jew's in non-Jew's house with Jew's liability — permitted even rabbinically — not present in your hand since body is non-Jew's and house is non-Jew's. Thus leniency for us: whatever no prohibition to retain — only rabbinically like nokshah or chametz nullified before witnesses with coercion — Jerusalem Pesachim R' Yosi forbids only due to evasion; non-Jew who lent to Jew after Passover forbidden — Jew transgresses bal yera'eh; Ramban and Ran — non-Jew who lent to Jew after Passover forbidden though no bal yera'eh since fit to transgress — rabbinically forbidden to retain — penalty; nokshah different since cannot come to bal yera'eh — see at length siman 443.
peri-megadim/4:ב: And he transgresses — apparently proof from mishnah; see there at length in eshel avraham.
peri-megadim/4:ג: And the depositor — see Chok Yaakov and Chacham Tzvi and Panim Me'irot cited in Baer Heitev.
peri-megadim/4:ד: He transgresses — both; see Mishna Berurah there.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif 1 — if he is liable for it. Meaning he accepted explicitly, for we hold there is no law of guardians for a non-Jew. And even if he accepted explicitly to be obligated in payment — some say for negligence it helps without kinyan but for theft and loss kinyan is required — see Gilyon Choshen Mishpat siman 291 s.k. 27 and Machaneh Efraim Hilchot Shomrim siman 8.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 1 — that even if the non-Jew comes it is permitted on Passover; in my opinion: since the Jew transgressed bal yera'eh when the non-Jew came on Passover he may not leave it for him to take; although not called benefiting — nevertheless the Jew is obligated to destroy to fix the negative commandment, for bal yera'eh is transformed to a positive as in Pesachim 95a; thus he must burn and pay the non-Jew his money.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: He must destroy it. See Baer Heitev; see responsum Sha'agat Aryeh siman 87 and Avnei Nezer that nullification and hefker do not help for others' chametz for which he accepted liability — this does not remove bal yera'eh; no remedy except burning or designating a house or partition ten handbreadths before Passover. He wrote in siman 79 and 80 — if he did not make this remedy until within Passover — forbidden in benefit after Passover; but if he made the remedy before six hours even for non-Jew's and there is a positive commandment of tashbitu from six hours — nevertheless although he transgressed the positive of tashbitu — permitted in benefit after Passover — see there extensive cases siman 83, 84, Beit Efraim siman 41, etc.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Another non-Jew. See Baer Heitev; see Sha'agat Aryeh siman 85 — chametz of a non-Jew deposited with another non-Jew — even if the second did not transgress bal yera'eh — permitted in benefit after Passover.
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: And there are those who disagree. See Baer Heitev — meaning even though one may not rely on Kaf HaChayim regarding compelling non-Jew b'dieved, nevertheless on the first view requiring explicit liability for theft and loss one may rely b'dieved — so Kaf HaChayim; thus I answered questioners on Baer Heitev; see Sha'agat Aryeh siman 88 — accepted only negligence liability — although must destroy before Passover, if he transgressed and did not destroy — permitted in benefit after Passover — see there.
shaarei-teshuvah/4:_: Not. See Baer Heitev; see Tiferet Tzvi — if soldiers stand in a Jew's house and he cannot make a partition — nevertheless need not leave his house, for whatever is not deposit law we are not concerned he will eat from it, as Rashba; even if not in his house, since he is in the city like wine deposit — on a day he does not come to his house he truly covers with a vessel since partition impossible — see there.
turei-zahav/1:_: But he knows the non-Jew is forceful, etc. — and there are those who disagree. Beit Yosef brought two views — Rambam and Raavad: Rambam holds if the non-Jew is forceful it is as his own and he must destroy, explaining Rava to sons of Machoza — warriors' chametz is stringent since if stolen they will compel payment though payments were not by law but under duress — nevertheless called their chametz; Raavad holds liability from duress is not liability obligating biur; Rava there was legal liability from kingdom law to support soldiers guarding the city. Challenge on Rambam: why does Gemara need verse to teach where liable it is as his own — per view gorem lemamon not as money we need to teach regarding chametz anyway forbidden; per view as money — why need verse for duress; further challenge on Rava — why say burn, sell suffices; why give to another non-Jew — does not help, especially per Rama; why Rava said "in your city from your houses" — should say briefly "in your city warriors' chametz"; for Raavad — give to another non-Jew and exempt from king's law; for Rambam — even giving to another non-Jew he will compel payment — difficult; Gemara "accepted liability" does not imply Jew accepted liability for duress — how bring proof from Rava; thus one who rules like Raavad did not lose due to these difficulties.
turei-zahav/2:_: And he must make, etc. — and although he did not accept liability, if he accepted liability partition does not help; even designating a house does not help — Rambam and Rashi and R' Tam; R' Tam holds even with liability designating a house helps, and partition helps; without liability no partition needed. Why then does designation help with liability — why did Rava say "in your city from your houses" — should say designated place; one may say he truly told them to destroy from their designated houses and take to warriors' place. R' Tam — with liability must designate explicitly; if only "here is the house" since he accepted liability he would have to pay if he did not designate — when he clarifies we say it is clarified, for we do not say birur in a d'oraisa matter.
turei-zahav/4:_: A Jew who deposited, etc. — in Asheri Pesachim ch. 1: some say Jew who deposited with Jew or non-Jew with guardian's acceptance — guardian liable not depositor since not in his domain; proof from mechilta "in your houses" — your house in your domain, excluding non-Jew's chametz in Jew's domain who cannot destroy, excluding Jew's chametz in non-Jew's domain not in his domain. R' Yonah — obligation on depositor; proof from stolen from man's house not temple — unclear; he did not explain mechilta; it appears when guardian lent his house for guarding depositor's money we call it depositor's house — mechilta regarding non-Jew who lent to Jew; challenge on first case; Ran on Rambam — transgresses and source unknown; perhaps only with liability; perhaps Rambam only theft and loss; here likewise depositor; Raavan — geonim: with acceptance guardian liable not depositor; primary reason — not in domain; both transgress if accepted; there unpaid guardian; Rosh — guardian destroys; Tur — geonim: since accepted liability; Beit Yosef — Ramban and Ran; Ran and Ramban explain like R' Tam; Jew's chametz in non-Jew's house with liability — why no transgress (excluded); rabbinically forbidden; Jew lent to non-Jew after Passover transgresses; non-Jew's in non-Jew's house with Jew's liability — no transgress even rabbinically; R' Tam — not found except not present; Rosh — depositor transgresses for Jew's in non-Jew's house with liability; permitted for non-Jew's in non-Jew's house. Practical leniency; Jerusalem R' Yosi — evasion; siman 443 explained; appears when depositor present; if not — guardian acts as siman 443 seif 2 — see there.
yad-ephraim/1:_: Taz s.k. 1 — if so why does Gemara challenge the other version; apparently one may say if as money automatically likewise for duress; possibly Raavad agrees for those who hold as money he is liable even when gorem lemamon from duress — he argues only for those who hold not as money, only because "not found" — Raavad holds only where obligation is by law; Rambam holds even for duress; Taz appears to hold certainly for those who hold as money — from logic since liability rests on him it is as his own — only where obligation is by law, not duress where chametz still exists no liability name and if lost he is exempt and payment is separate duress not entering his domain; not gorem lemamon; Rambam holds even for duress since cannot say acceptance makes it his when not as money — obligation of biur only from "not found" — whatever under Jew's hand must destroy — verse excludes others' without his liability; includes when liability on him even from duress; Taz's challenge on verse and giving to another non-Jew; Rama even re-deposit — Taz holds even second non-Jew's acceptance does not help unlike Magen Avraham; "all the more" possibly typo.
yad-ephraim/2:_: There — how bring proof from Rava; apparently difficult — all the more from Rava since even for compelling liable, all the more legal liability; possibly Taz means "accepted liability" means Jew accepted on himself; "did not accept" means did not accept on himself but still liable for duress — how bring proof from Rava; forced; possibly emend — no proof to Rava, meaning sugya "like Rava" supports what Rava said; per wording "accepted" not support for Rava.
yad-ephraim/3:_: There s.k. 4 — but per gorem lemamon as money no novelty; see Mishbetzot — challenge on sugya "not found" why needed; per view as money also novelty; Taz intent: for not as money — novelty even in conclusion different from general not as money — here considered as his own — "your houses" on novelty; for as money — only where stolen and gorem; where not yet stolen and still exists — thought not gorem — verse teaches included; whence learn generally gorem as money even while exists; "your houses" on novelty; truly no novelty since generally likewise — verse teaches not to err; only where generally truly not as money we say verse teaches novelty; although here novel as money in his hand, not for as money — since verse revealed even while exists as money we learn generally — no distinction; exclusion in your houses on all — in my opinion.
